.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dry conditions persist through the work week, with temperatures
  trending warmer. 
- A weak cold front arrives on Sunday and Sunday night.
- Wetter conditions late Monday through early Wednesday, possibly
  drier for Thanksgiving.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1201 PM CST Wed Nov 18 2026

Upper level ridging remains the core wx feature driving conditions 
across SE Texas now throughout the next several days. High pressure 
remains situated over the Eastern Conus with a sfc trough over the 
Gulf. These two features have created a tight pressure gradient, 
which will continue to bring periods hazardous marine conditions 
through at least Thursday. In addition, this sfc trough has also 
created a small convergence zone, resulting in some light showers 
developing off the coast. Still, low PWs and ridging should keep the 
rest of the region dry now into at least the early weekend. Highs 
this afternoon will be in the upper 60s/mid 70s with lows for 
Thursday morning in the upper 40s/50s inland and lower 60s along the 
coast. Temperatures should gradually warm over the next several days 
with highs reaching the 70s by Saturday and lows climbing into the 
50s/60s.

A shortwave trough is expected to sweep across the Southern Plains 
on Sunday, sending a weak cold front towards SE Texas. This weak 
front should be off the coast by early Monday morning. The tail end 
of the forecast gets a bit messy. A coastal trough may develop 
around the Texas coastal bend on Tuesday from the remnants of the 
weak front. Additional disturbances passing through the central 
CONUS Tuesday/Wednesday could inject another shot of cool/dry air 
into the region. The 06z Deterministic GFS comes off as a stark 
outlier amongst the slew of deterministic guidance, being distinctly 
wetter through Thanksgiving. Other deterministic guidance like the 
ICON & EURO, along with a slew of ensemble guidance from the LREF 
and ECMWF suggest much drier wx for Wednesday & onwards. Even within 
the GFS ensemble, a plethora of members from the 06z run are 
distinctly drier. The 12z run has backed off slightly, now shifting 
the timing of this wet period moreso into Friday. Cannot rule out 
rain entirely for Thanksgiving, though current signs suggests 
broadly drier conditions during that period. Regardless, the 
forecast can still change over these next few days, so stay tuned 
for updates, especially with regards to Thanksgiving. 

03

&&

.AVIATION...
(00Z TAF Issuance)
Issued at 528 PM CST Wed Nov 18 2026

Conditions will gradually deteriorate late this evening/tonight, 
dropping from MVFR to possibly IFR levels due to fog and/or low 
clouds. Pockets of MVFR ceilings remain over coastal counties, 
including LBX and should persist through the late evening. Further
inland, fog will be the primary hazard across the terminals, 
particularly between 09Z-14Z Thursday. Conditions are expected to 
gradually improve by mid.late Thursday morning, returning to VFR 
levels alongside light northeast winds. 

JM 

&&

.MARINE...
Issued at 1201 PM CST Wed Nov 18 2026

Northeast winds near 20 knots and seas of 5-8 feet are expected over 
the Gulf waters through Thursday. A Small Craft Advisory remains in 
effect for the offshore water (20-60nm) through late Thursday night. 
Winds and seas decrease into Friday with light northeast to east 
winds expected through Saturday. A weak cold front may push off the 
coast some time late Sunday night/early Monday morning with moderate 
N/NE winds possible in its wake.
